The observed cross-psalm echo to web:Ps.31.3 is independently re-collated: oshb:Ps.71.3's closing clause כִּֽי סַלְעִ֖י וּמְצוּדָתִ֣י אָֽתָּה and oshb:Ps.31.4's כִּֽי סַלְעִ֣י וּמְצוּדָתִ֣י אָ֑תָּה share identical consonants at skeleton tier (cantillation/vocalic pointing differ only) - correctly disclosed as texture, not the seam driver. Confidence high matches the strength of the imperative-cluster/causal-pivot evidence.

You are my God since my mother bore me.”, matching the row's quoted fragments exactly; dual-cite arithmetic web:22.9=oshb:22.10 and web:22.10=oshb:22.11 confirmed via ps_lib. The end-seam at v.8|v.9 is independently confirmed: v.9 introduces 'old age'/'strength fails' vocabulary with no prior occurrence in vv.1-8, a genuine lexical-shift tier-1 marker, which the one-sentence rejected_alternative correctly cites. unit_type strophe is correct. Confidence medium is a defensible, non-overreaching calibration for a seam resting on a causal conjunction rather than a stronger disjunctive or vocative marker.

v.9's 'old age'/'strength fails' opener is confirmed as new-to-the-psalm vocabulary against vv.1-8. The span coheres as one petition-report-quoted taunt-counter petition-imprecation complex: v.10 reports the conspiracy, v.11 is quoted enemy speech (a genuine discourse frame), v.12 returns to direct petition, v.13 closes with imprecation against the same threat. The rejected_alternative correctly identifies and rejects the most tempting internal break (after v.11's taunt), reasoning that vv.12-13 continue addressing the same conspiracy without a new vocative or topic shift - checked and concurred. Independently checked oshb:Ps.71.12's ketiv/qere pair against pmarks_Ps.json (kq['Ps.71.12'] = 1 note): the staged bytes show לְעֶזְרָ֥תִי חישה חֽוּשָׁה, a ketiv/qere spelling doublet of the same imperative 'hurry' with no semantic difference; the row's English quote of this verse ('My God, hurry to help me') rests on no material distinction between the two readings, so non-disclosure here is not a defect. unit_type strophe correct; confidence high matches the vocabulary-shift and discourse-frame evidence.

Re-ran the byte-tier collation of the opener וַ֭אֲנִי against oshb:Ps.71.14 independently (collate.py reports tier=byte), confirming the row's strongest claim: an explicit adversative pivot directly following the imprecation of v.13, the strongest seam in the cluster. The end-seam at v.18|v.19 is corroborated by v.19's own fronted-topic opener and doubled Elohim vocative plus the 'who is like you' incomparability formula - a real, if comparatively softer, tier-1 marker than v.14's adversative. rejected_alternative (extending through v.21) correctly identifies this. unit_type strophe correct; confidence high is justified by the byte-tier adversative-particle evidence.

The v.18|v.19 seam and v.21|v.22 seam are independently corroborated (v.19's fronted righteousness-clause opener plus doubled Elohim vocative plus the 'who is like you' formula; v.22's fronted 'also I' opener paralleling v.14's adversative 'but I', plus the instrument-naming register shift). unit_type strophe is correct and confidence medium is a fair, non-overreaching calibration for the softer (conjunctive rather than adversative) opening seam. However, the row quotes web:Ps.71.20 in its rationale without disclosing that oshb:Ps.71.20 carries a ketiv/qere fork that materially changes the verse's grammatical voice.

challenges.claim: The row quotes web:Ps.71.20 without disclosing that oshb:Ps.71.20 carries a ketiv/qere fork materially affecting the verse's grammatical number (communal 'us' vs individual 'me'), not merely an orthographic variant.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json kq inventory lists "Ps.71.20": 2 (two ketiv/qere notes, the book's maximum per verse). The staged bytes (verse_map_oshb.json) show both instances inline: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הראיתנו הִרְאִיתַ֨נִי צָר֥וֹת רַבּ֗וֹת וְרָ֫ע֥וֹת תָּשׁ֥וּב תחיינו תְּחַיֵּ֑ינִי וּֽמִתְּהֹמ֥וֹת הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ תָּשׁ֥וּב תַּעֲלֵֽנִי - ketiv הראיתנו/תחיינו (1st-common-plural 'us') vs qere הִרְאִיתַ֨נִי/תְּחַיֵּ֑ינִי (1st-common-singular 'me') - a communal-vs-individual-voice fork, not a spelling-only doublet (contrast oshb:Ps.71.12's ketiv/qere, which is orthographic-only). The row's own field quotes this verse in English (“You, who have shown us many and bitter troubles, you will let me live. You will bring us up again from the depths of the earth.”, web:Ps.71.20) with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in the row, despite the toolkit's stated rule that K/Q verses are disclosed when quoted.

The closing inclusio claim is verified: v.13's and v.24's shame-vocabulary share the same root at skeleton tier, correctly hedged by the writer as an 'echo' rather than a verbatim repeat, since the verb forms differ (jussive vs. perfect). The span closes the psalm and its parent grouping exactly at v.24, the book's confirmed last verse of Ps 71 (24=24 per the offset map); check_tiling independently confirms the full 6-row set tiles Ps.71.1-24 exactly with no gaps or overlaps. rejected_alternative (starting at v.23 instead) is one sentence and correctly identifies v.22's named-instrument register shift as the reason the row starts at v.22. unit_type strophe and confidence high are both well supported.
